mechanism_narrative: The four-week monotonic decline in RETAIL_REC from -11.6 to -22.9 reflects a weakening discretionary mobility regime, and this downward momentum will extend into the next four weeks because no other series shows a sustained rebound sufficient to reverse it.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -11.6 to -22.9 over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is greater than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The joint recovery of WORKPLACES from -59.0 to -32.0 and TRANSIT from -56.4 to -55.9 signals that commuting and station footfall are normalizing; this commuting recovery will lift weekday retail-and-recreation visits, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -59.0 to -32.0 over t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days when WORKPLACES is above -30% and TRANSIT is above -50%.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility at +12.7% keeps consumers at home and suppresses discretionary retail trips; when RESIDENTIAL crosses below +10.0%, the at-home constraint weakens and RETAIL_REC increases over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has remained above +12% for the last three weeks
failure_condition: After RESIDENTIAL falls below +10.0%, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The collapse in PARKS from +21.6% to -8.9% over three weeks indicates a seasonal shift away from outdoor recreation; consumers substitute toward indoor retail-and-recreation, raising RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from +21.6 to -8.9 over t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than or equal to its mean over the last 7 days while PARKS remains below 0.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, deep transit suppression and workplace avoidance force retail closures and trip reductions; while TRANSIT stays below -50% and WORKPLACES remains below -40%, RETAIL_REC will fall over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has been below -55% for three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES is below -40% and TRANSIT is below -50%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM falling from +10.7% to +1.9% shows that precautionary shopping is unwinding; as grocery/pharmacy trips normalize, consumers reallocate trips to discretionary retail, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from +10.7 to +1.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days after GROCERY_PHARM falls below +2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of a still-elevated RESIDENTIAL series and a recovering but negative WORKPLACES series signals a persistent work-from-home regime that reduces commuting-linked retail trips; this interaction will keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remains above +12% while WORKPLACES remains below -30%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days while RESIDENTIAL is above +12% and WORKPLACES is below -30%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT stations have been stuck below -55% for three weeks, capping station-area retail footfall; if TRANSIT crosses above -50%, the release of suppressed transit demand will raise RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved only from -56.4 to -55.9 over t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: After TRANSIT crosses above -50%, RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than its mean over the last 7 days.
